reviewMode: Independent. Refute, not confirm. Every digest, mode, byte, quote and current-standing claim recomputed from live disk at review time.
verdictRule: ACCEPT only if no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX. Two MUST-FIX survive verification, so the verdict is REJECT.
verdictBasis: The copy act itself is sound. The subject moves no frozen anchor, invents no bound and no platform list, closes no leftover-design, collapses no lineage, and lands the g21-fixture-corpus.v22 Codex SHOULD-FIX exactly as dispatched. The dispatched attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' lands: the subject pins docs/coop/artifacts/g21-fixture-corpus.v22.review-independent.claude2.json at bab65f34..., while live bytes hash to 0fc9a9fa.... Reading those live bytes shows the mismatch is not cosmetic: the live predecessor review records verdict REJECT with a labeled SHOULD-FIX and 5 observations, whereas the subject records it in four places as 'ACCEPT 0/0; 8 unlabeled observations'. Both the digest pin and the verdict characterisation are contradicted by the bytes they cite, so both are MUST-FIX.

findings.title: The pinned digest for the g21-fixture-corpus.v22 Claude Stage A review does not load-equal live bytes.
findings.measurement: Both locations pin bab65f349374dd8ed571f67bfd05ee8146f0e8f763f721469e55d7843f15f516. The live file hashes to 0fc9a9fa1a765d40bf05bba1cfe862c8b47ede9cb9e95bc9fafa71953f830f15, confirmed with two independent hashers. It is the only one of 42 path-to-digest pairs in the subject that fails; the other 41, including the subject itself, the four fixture copies, the frozen source payload, file 08, COORD, occupancy v4, control-protocol-contract.v2 and every other cited review, all load-equal. The file is also the only cited review at mode 0644; the other eleven cited reviews are 0444. Its mtime is 2026-09-01 01:30:23, five minutes before the subject was written at 01:35:01 and seven minutes before the review prompt at 01:35:37, so the divergence predates dispatch rather than following it.
findings.whyMustFix: recordedInputs is the subject's evidence spine, and the dispatched attack list names 'cited digests do not match live bytes' as a disqualifying condition. The subject's own remeasurementClause commands remeasurement before recording whenever a cited file moves in a way that is not append-only COORD growth or COORD heading hygiene. Recording g21-fixture-corpus.v23 with this pin would put a digest into the register that no reader can reproduce from disk.

findings.title: The recorded g21-fixture-corpus.v22 Claude Stage A verdict is contradicted by the live bytes of the review it cites.
findings.measurement: The subject records the predecessor Claude Stage A outcome as 'ACCEPT 0/0; 8 unlabeled observations', repeats 'Claude ACCEPT 0/0' in basedOn.predecessorV22.role, scopes purpose to landing the 'Codex 1 unlabeled SHOULD-FIX' alone, and asserts at findingDisposition.claudeV22Observations that the review 'returned 8 unlabeled observation strings'. The live file records verdict REJECT, counts {MUST-FIX 0, SHOULD-FIX 1, ADVISORY 1, OBSERVATION 5}, one finding carrying the explicit identifier CLAUDE-G21FXV22-S-1, one advisory CLAUDE-G21FXV22-A-1, and five observations. Every element of the subject's characterisation is wrong: the verdict (REJECT, not ACCEPT), the SHOULD-FIX count (1, not 0), the label status (labeled, not unlabeled), and the observation count (5, not 8).
findings.whyMustFix: basedOn is a custody record of what prior review actually decided. Recording g21-fixture-corpus.v23 at a D-000 heading would enter a false prior-verdict statement into the register, and would represent a REJECT as an ACCEPT. It also understates the landing set: purpose claims to land one Codex SHOULD-FIX when the live predecessor record carries a Claude SHOULD-FIX as well.
findings.repairDoesNotRequireNewBytes: The remediation itself is already present. Live CLAUDE-G21FXV22-S-1 is the same defect class as the Codex SHOULD-FIX, namely bare leftover-join version tokens in registerRowNote and remeasurementClause, and the subject repairs it: the two clauses gained three 'of G21' insertions each, so leftover-join.v21 of G21, leftover-join.v22 of G21, leftover-join.v23 of G21 and leftover-join.v24 of G21 are now qualified separately. Only the attribution is wrong.
findings.repair: Restate basedOn.predecessorV22.reviews.claude.verdict and basedOn.predecessorV22.role from live bytes, widen purpose to name both landed SHOULD-FIX findings, and rewrite findingDisposition.claudeV22Observations to the live observation count. The Claude finding already carries CLAUDE-G21FXV22-S-1 in its own bytes, so citing that identifier quotes a real label and invents nothing.
findings.identifierDiscipline: This finding invents no identifier. The Codex g21-fixture-corpus.v22 SHOULD-FIX is confirmed unlabeled in live bytes and stays unlabeled here. No observation identifier is invented for any predecessor observation string.

advisories.note: Both clauses read 'the v21 payload digest' while fixtures/g21.v21/ is also the directory this speaker authors, so the bare v21 token carries two live referents. The intended g21-fixture-corpus.v21 referent is fully qualified at authoredCatalog.members[0].mutation, and the token does not collide with this artifact's version integer, so the subject's own failsIf clause on bare version tokens is not tripped. Live CLAUDE-G21FXV22-A-1 raised the same point against the predecessor and it remains unaddressed; it is advisory-grade in both places.

advisories.note: The systemic cause of CLAUDE-G21FXV23-M-1 is that docs/coop/artifacts/g21-fixture-corpus.v22.review-independent.claude2.json was left writable at 0644 while every other cited review is frozen at 0444. Freezing each review output to 0444 at write time, the way subjects and fixture bytes already are, closes the class rather than this instance.
